# read


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Many PDFs carry a text layer, the text you can select and copy. When the
PDF was made from a digital document that layer is exact and costs
nothing to read. A scanned PDF has no text layer, or one made by OCR
(optical character recognition) that may be poor. Old books in Indian
scripts are often worse: many were set in legacy fonts whose text layer
reads as Latin gibberish, or splits akṣaras, the letter clusters of
Devanagari, apart. A vision model, one that reads images, can read such
a page from its picture, but it costs time or money for every page and
makes mistakes of its own.

[`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc)
decides page by page, and `parse` sets the route:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>parse=</code></th>
<th>what each page gets</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>auto</code>, the default</td>
<td>a text layer that passes the checks below is kept; a scanned page is
OCRed; a page still scanned or flagged after that goes to
<code>model</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>text</code></td>
<td>the text layer only; a scanned page stays empty</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ocr</code></td>
<td>OCR on every page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>llm</code></td>
<td><code>model</code> on every page</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`model` is any id Urai knows, local or hosted, such as `claude/sonnet`
or `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`; None means `$VISHALAKSHI_MODEL`. There are
two ways in. The function `read_doc(path)` reads one file and returns
its pages, with no vault involved. `Vault.read_doc(src)` reads a file,
or every PDF and image under a folder, into the vault: each file becomes
one document, and each page’s text, route and flags are kept as numbered
versions, so reading a page again never loses an earlier reading.

## Prompts

A vision model is told what to return by a reading prompt. `PRESETS`
holds four. Each asks for the page as JSON: a list of items in reading
order, where an item is a heading, a paragraph of prose, a verse, a
table, a note or a colophon (the line that closes a chapter in an Indian
text), with its text exactly as printed and any number printed with it.
Once read, these items are called blocks. `generic` suits any printed
page. `sanskrit` and `tamil` name the letters that old prints in those
scripts make easy to misread, and `sanskrit` also tells the model to
leave out translation and commentary. `tables` reads tables as rows of
cells.

Every preset also asks for a `box` per item: the region it covers, as
`[x0, y0, x1, y1]` in fractions of the page’s width and height measured
from the top left, so an app can crop the block out of the page image or
highlight it.

[`reading_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#reading_prompt)
fills a preset in with the document’s `title`, its `script` (Devanagari
unless you say otherwise) and a `hint`, a sentence about this particular
book, such as how it numbers its verses or what to skip. A `preset` that
is not one of the four names is used as the whole prompt. If it contains
`{of}`, `{title}`, `{script}` or `{hint}` they are filled in, and a
prompt whose JSON braces are not doubled is sent unchanged.


*Fill in the reading prompt `name` with the title, script and hint, or
use `name` itself as the prompt when it is not a preset.*

``` python
assert 'Gita' in reading_prompt('sanskrit', 'Gita') and 'ष look like प' in reading_prompt('sanskrit')
assert 'Tamil' in reading_prompt('tamil')
assert all('"box": [x0, y0, x1, y1]' in reading_prompt(k) and 'leave it out' in reading_prompt(k) for k in PRESETS)
test_eq(reading_prompt('Read it: {hint}', hint='x'), 'Read it: x')
test_eq(reading_prompt('A {script} page of {title}. {{"items": []}} {hint}', 'Gita', 'Tamil'), 'A Tamil page of Gita. {"items": []} ')
test_eq(reading_prompt('Return {"items": []} only.', 'Gita'), 'Return {"items": []} only.')   # no template: as it is
```

## Pages as images

A model is sent a picture of the page.
[`render`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#render)
draws one page of a PDF as a PNG at `dpi` (200 by default). Some hosted
models refuse large images, so when the PNG is over `max_bytes` (3 MB)
[`render`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#render)
returns a JPEG whose long side fits `max_px` (3,000 pixels) instead, and
[`fit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#fit) does
the same for an image file. Two cuts help with hard pages.
[`halves`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#halves)
splits a landscape image, usually a scan of two facing pages (a spread),
into its left and right pages.
[`page_strips`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#page_strips)
cuts a tall page into overlapping horizontal strips, so the model sees
worn or small type at a larger scale.

``` python
from pdf_oxide import Pdf
_fx = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
for _i, _t in enumerate(['# Attention Is All You Need\n\nThe dominant sequence transduction models are based on recurrent or convolutional networks.',
                         '# Background\n\nThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU.']):
    Pdf.from_markdown(_t).save(str(_fx/f'p{_i}.pdf'))
Pdf.merge([str(_fx/'p0.pdf'), str(_fx/'p1.pdf')]).save(str(_fx/'two.pdf'))
_src = _fx/'two.pdf'
_png = render(_src, 0, dpi=72)
assert _png[:4] == b'\x89PNG'
assert render(_src, 0, dpi=300, max_bytes=1000)[:2] == b'\xff\xd8'   # over the limit: a JPEG
test_eq(fit(_png), _png); assert fit(_png, 100, 1000)[:2] == b'\xff\xd8'
from PIL import Image
def _size(b): return Image.open(io.BytesIO(b)).size
_w, _h = _size(_png)
test_eq(halves(_png), [_png])                                   # a portrait page is one page
_b = io.BytesIO(); Image.new('L', (200, 100), 255).save(_b, 'PNG'); _spread = _b.getvalue()
test_eq([_size(x) for x in halves(_spread)], [(100, 100), (100, 100)])
test_eq([_size(x) for x in page_strips(_png, 3)], [(_w, int(_h/3 + .06*_h)), (_w, int(2*_h/3 + .06*_h) - int(_h/3 - .06*_h)), (_w, _h - int(2*_h/3 - .06*_h))])
```

## Checks

[`flags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#flags)
lists what looks wrong with a page’s text. It is how `parse='auto'`
decides that a text layer cannot be trusted.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>flag</th>
<th>meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>thin</code></td>
<td>fewer than <code>min_chars</code> (20) letters, as on a scanned
page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>replacement</code></td>
<td>the Unicode replacement character, which marks text that failed to
decode</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>legacy</code></td>
<td>more than 5 Latin-1 or typographic characters per 100 letters, which
is how a legacy Devanagari font’s text layer reads</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>split</code></td>
<td>a line that starts with a vowel sign or virāma, a piece of an akṣara
cut off from the rest</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>akshara</code></td>
<td>an akṣara that cannot be written, such as a virāma followed by a
vowel sign</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>foreign</code></td>
<td>Greek or Cyrillic letters next to Devanagari</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`disagree(a, b)` measures how far two readings of the same text differ:
the letter edits between them divided by the letters in the longer one.
Spaces, digits, daṇḍas and punctuation are ignored and vowel signs
count. A value of 0.1 or more is worth a look.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vishalakshi/blob/main/vishalakshi/read.py#L114"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
test_eq(flags('Hello world this is enough letters'), [])
test_eq(flags('क्ा and more letters here to pass'), ['akshara'])
assert 'split' in flags('कृष्ण\nा is a sign broken off here, long enough')
assert 'legacy' in flags('Jke ‘kfDr ¼ji¼ Hkxoku ¾ ™ more text here')
test_eq(flags(''), ['thin'])
assert disagree('रामः', 'रामा') > 0 and disagree('राम ॥१॥', 'राम') == 0
test_eq(disagree('', ''), None)
```

## Reading a page

[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
sends one page image to a vision model and returns its `blocks`, their
text joined as markdown (`text`), the `model` and the `cost` its backend
reported. With no `chat=`, the call goes through
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat),
so each reading is recorded once and replayed after that, and reading
the same page again costs nothing. The recordings go in `chatcache` in
the working directory, or the folder `$VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE` names. A
page that has no recording yet reaches the model only when
`$VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT` is set; otherwise
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
raises an error that says so. `fresh=True` drops the recorded reply and
asks the model again. A reply that is not JSON raises an error and is
not recorded, so the next try reaches the model. `chat=` takes any
callable in place of a model, which is how the tests run without one,
and every image sent is first held to the size limit by
[`fit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#fit).

A block keeps its `box` only when it is four numbers that make a real
rectangle, clamped to the page; any other box is dropped.
[`crop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#crop) cuts
a block out of the page image by its box.

Before sending,
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
asks
[`send_rule`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#send_rule)
whether the page may go, as an image. The page’s level is its document’s
level, raised to Personal when `text`, its text layer or OCR, holds an
identifier. A page image cannot be masked, so a Personal page goes to a
hosted model only with `allow=True` or `pii='off'`, and a Local only
page never does. A page that may not be sent comes back empty, with
`blocked` saying why.

``` python
class Fake:
    "A vision model stand-in: it answers every page with the same two items, in a code fence."
    model, calls = 'fake/vision', 0
    def __call__(self, msg):
        Fake.calls += 1
        return dict(content='```json\n{"items":[{"kind":"heading","text":"Attention Is All You Need"},{"kind":"prose","text":"The dominant sequence transduction models are based on recurrent networks."}]}\n```', usage=dict(cost=0.01))
_r = read_page(_png, chat=Fake())
test_eq([b['kind'] for b in _r.blocks], ['heading', 'prose'])
assert _r.text.startswith('## Attention') and _r.cost == .01
class Boxed(Fake):
    "A reader that gives boxes: one sane, one out of range, one reversed, one not a box."
    def __call__(self, msg):
        return dict(content=json.dumps(dict(items=[dict(kind='heading', text='Attention', box=[.1, .05, .9, .1]), dict(kind='prose', text='The dominant models', box=[-.1, .2, 1.2, .5]),
                                                   dict(kind='prose', text='are recurrent', box=[.9, .6, .1, .7]), dict(kind='note', text='x', box='top')])))
_r = read_page(_png, chat=Boxed())
test_eq([b.get('box') for b in _r.blocks], [[.1, .05, .9, .1], [0., .2, 1., .5], None, None])
from PIL import Image
_w, _h = Image.open(io.BytesIO(_png)).size
_c = crop(_png, [0, 0, .5, .5], pad=0)
test_eq((_c[:4], Image.open(io.BytesIO(_c)).size), (b'\x89PNG', (round(_w / 2), round(_h / 2))))
_cw, _ch = Image.open(io.BytesIO(crop(_png, [.4, .4, .6, .6]))).size
assert abs(_cw - .24 * _w) <= 1 and abs(_ch - .24 * _h) <= 1
test_eq(crop(_png, None), _png); test_eq(crop(_png, [.5, .5, .5, .6]), _png)
test_eq(_md([dict(kind='table', rows=[['a', 'b'], ['1', '2']])]), '| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |')
```

## Reading a document

`read_doc(path)` takes a PDF or a page image and returns one row per
page, `{page, text, route, flags}`, with `blocks`, `model` and `cost` on
a page the model read. `route` says how the text was got: `text` (the
text layer), `ocr`, `model`, or `scanned` when nothing read the page.
`pages=[...]` limits which pages may go to the model, and the others
keep their text layer. Up to `workers` pages (4) are read at once.

Privacy works page by page, as in
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page).
When any page is going to a model, the whole text layer is first checked
for a sensitive doctype, so a document whose text reads clearly as a
passport or a payslip is Local only before any page image leaves.
`local_model=`, or a built `local_chat=`, reads the pages that the
hosted `model` may not; without one those pages keep their text layer
and carry `blocked`. A scanned page has no text to check, so it is
judged by its document’s level alone.

Long reads need control:

- `progress(done, total, page, route, cost)` is called once with
  `done=0`, then after each page that was due for the model. Returning
  False stops the reading. The pages not yet read keep their text layer
  or OCR, the result’s `cancelled` is True and `unread` lists them. An
  error raised inside `progress` is ignored.
- `cache=` keeps each model reading as a JSON file,
  `{page, items, cost, model}`, in a folder (`p0001.json`, or
  `p0001a.json` and `p0001b.json` for the two halves of a spread) or
  wherever a function `cache(page, half)` says. A cached page is not
  sent again: its `cost` is None, since nothing was spent, and `cached`
  is True.
- `redo=[...]` reads those pages again even when cached. Once the new
  reading is saved, the old one moves to a sibling folder named after
  the cache folder with `_prev` added, numbered when an older copy is
  there already.
- `spread=True` treats a landscape page as two facing pages and reads
  the halves in turn. `strips=k` sends each image as `k` overlapping
  strips.
- `clean=` is a function applied to each block’s text before it is kept.
- `tries=n` tries a failing page up to `n` times, waiting `RETRY_WAIT`
  seconds (10) after the first failure, 20 after the second, and so on.
  A page that still fails keeps its text layer, carries its `error`, and
  is listed in the result’s `failed`. Without `tries`, the first error
  is raised.

`doc_cost(rows)` adds up the cost of the pages a model read, and
`doc_files(folder)` lists the PDFs and images under a folder.

``` python
_d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
_scan = _d/'scan.pdf'; _scan.write_bytes(pdf_doc(pdf_doc(_src).extract_pages_to_bytes([0])).flatten_to_images(dpi=150))
Fake.calls = 0
_t = read_doc(_src, chat=Fake(), out=_d/'.out')
test_eq(_t.attrgot('route'), ['text', 'text']); test_eq(Fake.calls, 0)          # a sound text layer goes to no model
_s = read_doc(_scan, parse='text', out=_d/'.out'); test_eq(_s[0].route, 'scanned')
_m = read_doc(_scan, parse='llm', chat=Fake(), out=_d/'.out')
test_eq(_m[0].route, 'model'); test_eq(_m[0].model, 'fake/vision')
(_d/'pg.png').write_bytes(_png)
test_eq(read_doc(_d/'pg.png', chat=Fake())[0].route, 'model')
test_eq(doc_files(_d).map(lambda f: f.name), ['pg.png', 'scan.pdf'])
```

``` python
# progress after each model page; False stops the rest, which keep their text layer

test_eq((doc_cost(_m), _m.cancelled, _m.unread), (.02, False, []))
_seen = []

assert 'Extended Neural GPU' in _m[1].text
```

``` python
# a spread read as its two pages, kept where `cache(page, half)` says; the page sent as strips; a failing page tried again, then left out
_spf = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'spread.png'; Image.new('L', (400, 200), 255).save(_spf)
class Halves(Fake):
    "Reads each image it is sent as the next half."
    def __call__(self, msg):
        Fake.calls += 1; Halves.msg = msg
        return dict(content=json.dumps(dict(items=[dict(kind='verse', text=f'half {Fake.calls}')])), usage=dict(cost=.5))
Fake.calls, _hd = 0, Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
_at = lambda page, half: _hd/f'p{page + 1:04d}{half or "a"}.json'
_m = read_doc(_spf, chat=Halves(), spread=True, cache=_at)
test_eq((_m[0].text, _m[0].cost, sorted(f.name for f in _hd.iterdir())), ('half 1\n\nhalf 2', 1., ['p0001a.json', 'p0001b.json']))
test_eq((read_doc(_spf, chat=Halves(), spread=True, cache=_at)[0].text, Fake.calls), ('half 1\n\nhalf 2', 2))
(_hd/'p0001b.json').unlink()   # one half kept is not the page: both read again, the old half set aside
test_eq((read_doc(_spf, chat=Halves(), spread=True, cache=_at)[0].text, Fake.calls, (_hd.parent/f'{_hd.name}_prev'/'p0001a.json').exists()), ('half 3\n\nhalf 4', 4, True))
_ppf = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'tall.png'; Image.new('L', (200, 400), 255).save(_ppf)   # a portrait page of a spread document is one reading, kept whole
read_doc(_ppf, chat=Halves(), spread=True, cache=(_at2 := lambda page, half, d=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()): d/f'p{page + 1:04d}{half or "a"}.json'))
test_eq((read_doc(_ppf, chat=Halves(), spread=True, cache=_at2)[0].text, Fake.calls), ('half 5', 5))
read_doc(_d/'pg.png', chat=Halves(), strips=3)
test_eq((len(Halves.msg), 'overlapping strips' in Halves.msg[-1]), (4, True))
class Flaky(Fake):
    "Fails its first call, as a model starting slowly does."
    n = 0
    def __call__(self, msg):
        Flaky.n += 1
        if Flaky.n == 1: raise TimeoutError('slow start')
        return super().__call__(msg)
class Down(Fake):
    def __call__(self, msg): raise TimeoutError('down')
RETRY_WAIT = 0
_m = read_doc(_src, parse='llm', chat=Flaky(), out=_d/'.out', workers=1, tries=2)
test_eq((_m.failed, _m.attrgot('route'), [r.get('error') for r in _m]), ([], ['model', 'model'], [None, None]))
_m = read_doc(_src, parse='llm', chat=Down(), out=_d/'.out', workers=1, tries=2, pages=[0], cache=(_fd := Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())))
test_eq((_m.failed, _m[0].route, _m[0].error, (_fd/'p0001.json').exists()), ([0], 'text', 'TimeoutError: down', False))
test_fail(lambda: read_doc(_src, parse='llm', chat=Down(), out=_d/'.out', workers=1), contains='down')
RETRY_WAIT = 10
```

## Into the vault

`Vault.read_doc(src)` reads a file, or every PDF and image under a
folder, and adds each file to the vault as one document that search and
`ask` can reach like any other. It also keeps each page in the
`read_pages` table as a version. A page gets a new version only when its
text, route or blocks changed, so reading a file twice with the same
result adds nothing. Each new version is scanned for personal
information and its findings are filed against it (see
[pii](09_pii.ipynb)). A new document starts at the shelf’s floor, and
one already in the vault at its own level. `Vault.pages(doc_id)` gives
the latest version of each page, and `history=True` gives every version.
Every page read by a hosted model is written to the send log. The result
is the ingest result with `routes` (how many pages took each route),
`flagged`, `blocked`, `cost`, `model_pages`, `cancelled`, `unread` and
`failed` added.

`Vault.reparse(doc_id, pages=[...])` reads pages of a document again, by
default with the model (`parse='llm'`) and with the document’s own
preset, script and hint, files the new readings as new versions and
re-indexes the document. Use it when a page came out badly and a better
model should have it. `reparse` returns the pages it read, those whose
text `changed`, `blocked`, `cost`, `model_pages`, `cancelled` and
`unread`. Both methods take `progress`, and a cancelled `reparse` leaves
its unread pages as they were. When a folder is read with `cache=`, each
file caches in its own subfolder, named after the file.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vishalakshi/blob/main/vishalakshi/read.py#L376"

``` python
def reparse(
    doc_id:str, pages:NoneType=None, model:str=None, preset:str=None, script:str=None, hint:str=None,
    parse:str='llm', dpi:int=200, workers:int=4, chat:NoneType=None, pii:str='redact', allow:bool=False,
    local_model:str=None, local_chat:NoneType=None, progress:NoneType=None
)->dict:
```

*Read pages of a document again, all of them when `pages` is None, file

### Vault.read_doc

``` python
def read_doc(
    src, title:str=None, kind:str=None, parse:str='auto', model:str=None, preset:str='generic', script:str='',
    hint:str='', pages:NoneType=None, dpi:int=200, workers:int=4, chat:NoneType=None,
    pii:str='redact', # off|local|redact|refuse, per page; the document's level and the shelf's floor apply
    allow:bool=False, # allow once, for Personal pages
    local_model:str=None, # reads the pages a hosted `model` may not
    local_chat:NoneType=None, # a built local reader instead of `local_model`
    progress:NoneType=None, # `progress(done, total, page, route, cost)` per file; False stops the reading
    spread:bool=False, strips:int=1, cache:NoneType=None, redo:NoneType=None, clean:NoneType=None,
    tries:int=None, # as `read_doc`; a folder's files cache in `cache/<stem>`
    **kw
):
```

*Read a PDF, a page image or every one under a folder into the vault
page by page, keeping each page’s readings as versions.*
